subject: Materials Science
title: Porosity: The Gaps That Matter
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Porosity: The Gaps That Matter.

hook.text: A flower pot lets water seep through slowly. A porcelain cup holds coffee without a drip.

buildup.text: Porosity is the percentage of a ceramic body that's empty space — trapped air pockets.

discovery.text: High porosity means lightweight and insulating. Low porosity means dense and strong.

twist.text: Some porosity is intentional — bone scaffolds need pores so cells can grow into them.

climax.text: Insulating firebrick is 70% air — light enough to hold barehanded while glowing red-hot.

punchline.text: Sometimes the holes in a ceramic matter more than the solid.

quiz.question: Why is high porosity useful in insulating firebrick?
options: Air pockets trap heat, making it a poor conductor
The holes allow flames to pass through
